items.t: China's A-Shares Add $7 Trillion in Two Years — So Who Actually Won?
items.s: Shanghai's benchmark index has climbed 45% since September 2024, adding roughly 51 trillion yuan in market value. Yet many ordinary investors say they have little to show for the rally, a gap that reveals how unevenly Chinese stock gains are distributed.

items.t: Chinese Phone Giant Infinix Unveils World-First Gaming Controller and Cooling Dock
items.s: Infinix, the gaming-focused brand of Shenzhen-based Transsion, has launched two GT NX accessories: a controller with the world's first pixel-precision touchpad for shooters and a dock with built-in thermoelectric cooling. The launch signals a push by China's low-profile phone giants into high-margin mobile gaming gear.

items.t: Next-Gen Memory Breakthrough: 10 Billion Read-Write Cycles
items.s: A Chinese-led research team says it has fixed the durability flaw in ferroelectric memory, pushing devices past 10 billion read-write cycles. The advance could bring faster, power-sipping storage closer to everyday chips.

items.t: Tesla Teases New Roadster With Glowing Light Bar Ahead of October Debut
items.s: Tesla has released another teaser for its second-generation Roadster, showing only a front LED light strip. The electric supercar is set to be fully unveiled on October 2, Beijing time.

items.t: AI Takes Over Sophisticated Investment Scams
items.s: Chinese investors face new wave of AI-powered financial fraud as artificial intelligence enables more sophisticated 'pig butchering' scams that manipulate victims into transferring large sums.

items.t: China's Smartphone Giants Switch Chip Suppliers
items.s: Major Chinese phone makers OPPO and vivo unexpectedly switch to MediaTek chips for flagship models, signaling industry shifts amid intense competition.

items.t: Donkey Kong's Final Banana Bash Delights Gamers
items.s: Nintendo wraps up a year of themed events with the 'Banana Frenzy Carnival' expansion in Donkey Kong: Banana Bliss. The week-long event offers players non-stop challenges on the 1400th underground level.

items.t: Huawei's HarmonyOS Expands Beyond Phones
items.s: Huawei's HarmonyOS ecosystem grows with specialized apps and automotive integration, marking its expansion beyond smartphones into broader consumer electronics and smart mobility.

items.t: China's Coffee Capital Brews a Global Financial Stir
items.s: Shanghai has quietly become the world's most crowded coffee market, turning a daily caffeine habit into a fierce commercial arena. This beverage boom is now drawing major consumer-finance attention as global funds pour capital into domestic chains.

items.t: China's Quantum Leap: Leading the Next Computing Revolution
items.s: China's rapid advancements in quantum computing technology position it as a key player in the next frontier of computational science, with breakthroughs that could transform industries worldwide.

items.t: China's Running Revolution: Marathon Culture Blooms
items.s: Once a nation of cyclists, China has embraced running marathons with unprecedented enthusiasm, creating one of the world's largest and most vibrant running communities.

items.t: China Launches Satellite Internet Constellation
items.s: China successfully deployed another batch of low-earth orbit satellites, continuing its ambitious space-based internet project with the launch of 26 satellite groups.

items.t: China's C919: The Homegrown Airliner Taking to More Skies
items.s: Developed by COMAC, the C919 narrow-body jet is expanding from its first commercial routes into a growing fleet. Here is what makes China's flagship passenger plane tick — and what it is like to fly on one.

items.t: China's EV Exports Are Redrawing the Global Auto Map
items.s: China is now the world's largest vehicle exporter, led by electric and plug-in hybrid cars from BYD, Chery and a wave of younger brands — a shift with big consequences for car prices everywhere.

items.t: Blockbusters and Records: Chinese Animation Grows Up
items.s: From Ne Zha's record-smashing runs to a new wave of studios, Chinese animated films have become a box-office force at home — and are eyeing audiences abroad.

items.t: Tiangong: Life and Science Aboard China's Space Station
items.s: Permanently crewed by rotating teams of three taikonauts, the Tiangong station hosts hundreds of experiments — and is opening its modules to payloads from around the world.

items.t: China's Auto Industry Faces a Wave of New Models and Deals
items.s: A busy week in China's car market brought nine new model launches, a major restructuring between two state-owned automakers, and a shift in the Huawei-Seres partnership, signaling intensifying competition and consolidation.

items.t: China's Auto Repair Talent Gap Grows as EV Boom Accelerates
items.s: China's electric vehicle boom is creating a shortage of skilled repair technicians, with salaries doubling but positions still unfilled. The WorldSkills competition in Shanghai highlights the advanced skills needed for modern vehicles.

items.t: China's Electric Car Repair Shops Can't Find Enough Workers
items.s: As electric vehicles flood Chinese roads, repair shops are struggling to hire technicians who understand both mechanics and software. At the WorldSkills competition in Shanghai, young mechanics showed why the job now demands programming skills.

items.t: China's EV Repair Shortage: Double the Pay, Still No Takers
items.s: As electric vehicles flood Chinese roads, a severe shortage of qualified repair technicians is emerging. Fixing an EV now demands mechanical, electrical and software skills — and training pipelines are struggling to keep up.

items.t: One Day, Nine New Cars: Inside China's Crowded EV Market
items.s: On September 23, nine new models from brands like Geely, Changan and Denza hit Chinese showrooms in a single day. The pile-up reflects brutal competition in the world's largest car market, where too many models chase too few buyers.

items.t: Booker Prize 2026 Shortlist Unveiled, Celebrating Writing AI Cannot Copy
items.s: The 2026 Booker Prize shortlist, announced in London, features six novels from four countries, including two past winners and three first-time nominees. Chair of judges Mary Beard calls the list 'literary writing at its best,' highlighting works that resist AI replication.

items.t: China's AI Comic Drama Boom Meets Its First Big Shakeout
items.s: China's AI-generated comic dramas exploded to over 380,000 titles in eight months, but falling platform payouts triggered a 42% studio exit. The crisis echoes Japan's 1980s animation downturn, and creators are hunting for a sustainable model.

items.t: China's Box Office Buzz: Local Heroes and Global Classics
items.s: Chinese cinemas are rolling out a diverse slate this week, from the historical epic 'Dunhuang Heroes' to Quentin Tarantino's 'Kill Bill' re-release, while new comedies and thrillers keep audiences entertained.

items.t: China's Box Office This Week: Auteurs, Blockbusters and One Big Cast Reunion
items.s: Chinese cinemas are juggling a packed slate this week — from a Tang-dynasty epic to Nolan's Odyssey — while Hong Kong veterans Tony Leung Ka-fai and Yu Qian share the screen in a new crime comedy.

items.t: China's Screens Are Full of Stories — And One Big Goodbye
items.s: A beloved Chinese actor, You Benchang, died at 93, while cinemas fill with new releases from mainland China and Hollywood and short-form AI animation floods online platforms.

items.t: China's Sitcom Drought: Why the Laugh Track Fell Silent
items.s: A viral essay asks why China rarely produces hit sitcoms anymore, tracing the genre from 1993's 'I Love My Family' to 'iPartment' — and what streaming, censorship and short video changed.

items.t: China's ETF Market Hits New Milestone as Bond Funds Top $1 Trillion
items.s: China's bond exchange-traded funds have crossed the $1 trillion mark for the first time, while new stock indices launch for innovative drugs and software services. The milestone reflects growing investor appetite for diversified, low-cost investment tools in mainland markets.

items.t: Chinese Purification Equipment Maker Aims for IPO on Biotech Wave
items.s: Tianjin-based Oushangyuan has updated its listing prospectus for Shenzhen's ChiNext board, riding China's synthetic biology boom with clients including pharma giant Zhejiang NHU and food conglomerate COFCO. Its receivables have grown fast, drawing scrutiny.

items.t: Hong Kong Exchange to Accept Chinese Government Bonds as Collateral
items.s: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing will let traders pledge Chinese government and policy bank bonds held via Bond Connect as collateral from November 2026, deepening the bond market's global role and freeing up capital for derivatives trading.

items.t: Hong Kong Stocks Slide as Xiaomi Buys Back $640,000 in Shares
items.s: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell as much as 2% on Friday, dragging Chinese tech giants lower, while Xiaomi spent HK$50.1 million repurchasing its own shares. The pullback follows a softer night for US-listed Chinese stocks and rising Treasury yields.

items.t: Shanghai Exchange to Launch Two New Tech-Focused Stock Indexes
items.s: The Shanghai Stock Exchange and China Securities Index Co. will debut two new indexes on September 29, covering innovative drugmakers and software services. The move gives investors fresh tools to track China's fast-growing biotech and software sectors.

items.t: China's Deck-Building Hit 'Battle of the Golden Spatula' Turns Five With a Party
items.s: Tencent's auto-battler Battle of the Golden Spatula marked its fifth anniversary with a fan festival in Shenzhen, where players queued to swap handmade shovels for plush prizes. The mobile strategy game remains one of China's most-played titles.

items.t: China's Rayshine Studio Debuts New Hand-Drawn Fantasy Game at gamescom
items.s: Chinese indie developer Rayshine Studio unveiled The Order of Falling Stars, a hand-drawn fantasy adventure, at gamescom 2026, launching October 9 on PC, Switch 2 and PS5 for about $14. The game blends Chinese ink-wash art with action combat.

items.t: Chinese Studio Xishanju Sets October 15 Launch for Final 'Swordsman World'
items.s: Xishanju's Swordsman World 4: Infinite, the closing chapter of its long-running wuxia series, opens to all platforms on October 15. The studio also unveiled a cinematic trailer set in a war-torn ancient China.

items.t: Ninjala 2 Reinvents Itself as Open-World PvE Adventure at Tokyo Game Show
items.s: Six years after the original, Gungho's Ninjala 2 shifts from PvP battles to a PvE open-world action game with a full story mode and character progression. The game was showcased at Tokyo Game Show 2026, signaling a bold new direction for the colorful ninja franchise.

items.t: Swordman's Sequel 'JX World 4: Infinite' Sets October 15 Launch
items.s: Chinese studio Seasun will launch 'JX World 4: Infinite,' the finale of its long-running wuxia series, on October 15 across PC and mobile. A new cinematic trailer sets the story in a fractured Song dynasty.

items.t: Jonathan Blow's New Puzzle Epic 'Order of the Sinking Star' Priced at 98 Yuan
items.s: Legendary designer Jonathan Blow's next game, Order of the Sinking Star, arrives October 9 on PC, Switch 2 and PS5. Its China price of 98 yuan highlights how global studios now court Chinese players with regional pricing.

items.t: China's Home Coffee Bar: Inside the DIY Drink Craze
items.s: A popular Chinese tech-lifestyle site's fifth guide to homemade drinks shows how specialty coffee and mocktails have become a weekend ritual for young urban Chinese, moving café culture into the living room.

items.t: China's Home Coffee Bars: From Espresso to Creative Signature Drinks
items.s: A popular Chinese lifestyle guide shows how home mixologists craft cafe-style specialty coffee and drinks. It reflects a broader at-home beverage culture driven by affordable gear and social sharing.

items.t: China's Vision Pro Fans Rejoice: visionOS 27 Brings Big Upgrades
items.s: Apple's visionOS 27 update, released in September, adds Siri enhancements and new immersive environments to the Vision Pro headset. Chinese tech site SSPAI reports the changes bring a fresh feel to spatial computing.

items.t: Why One Chinese Writer Spent Ten Years Cataloguing Dead Computers
items.s: A decade-long project that began as a commercial experiment turned into a personal mission to document China's forgotten PCs. Its author now explains why he stopped calling himself a collector.

items.t: Where Earth's Extra Heat Really Goes: 91 Percent Into the Ocean
items.s: As China's solar capacity overtakes coal for the first time, scientists remind us that over 90 percent of trapped heat ends up in the ocean, not the air. The uneven warming explains why some regions feel the heat far more than others.

items.t: Why the Moon Looks Huge in Photos—and Tiny in Real Life
items.s: Every Mid-Autumn Festival, people photograph the full moon and wonder why it looks like a tiny glowing dot. Scientists say it comes down to how cameras, eyes and brains process the same light very differently.

items.t: Asian Games: China Sweeps Shot Put Gold as Records Tumble in Nagoya
items.s: China's Song Jiayuan won women's shot put gold with a season-best 19.40m, leading a 1-2 finish with teammate Zhang Linru at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. The day also brought a stunning 9.91-second men's 100m record and China's 95th gold.

items.t: Asian Games: China's Fencing Bronze, Table Tennis Wins, Skateboard Heartbreak
items.s: China's men's foil team lost a nail-biter to Japan 45-43 for bronze, while table tennis stars Lin Shidong and Wang Chuqin advanced to the round of 16. Skateboarder Chen Ye, the defending champion, finished last in the men's park final.

items.t: Asian Games Day Two: China's Shooters and Paddlers Shine in Hangzhou
items.s: China added gold in shooting and advanced its table tennis stars at the Hangzhou Asian Games, while the men's fencing team settled for bronze and skateboarding's defending champion slipped to eighth.

items.t: Swimmer Zhang Yufei Fires Back at Critics After Asian Games Gold
items.s: China's Zhang Yufei defended her 50m butterfly title at the Nagoya Asian Games, then hit back at online critics who said she was too old to keep competing. China's medal haul also passed 95 golds.

items.t: Teenager Breaks Asian Games 100m Record as China's Sprint Stars Survive Scare
items.s: A 20-year-old Thai sprinter shattered Su Bingtian's Asian Games 100m record with 9.91 seconds, while China's Xie Zhenye and Zeng Keli both advanced to a tense final in Nagoya.

items.t: China's Nio Completes 3,605km Silk Road Battery-Swap Route to Kazakhstan Border
items.s: Nio has opened its westernmost battery-swap station in Khorgos, completing a 3,605-kilometre corridor of 33 stations across China. The route lets drivers swap depleted batteries for fresh ones, reaching every provincial-level region without long charging stops.

items.t: F-Droid 2.0 Launches With a Cleaner Look and Smarter App Discovery
items.s: The free and open-source Android app store F-Droid has released version 2.0, rebuilding its interface around three simple areas: Discover, Search, and My Apps. The update also improves app discovery and management for privacy-conscious users worldwide.

items.t: Shift Up CEO Reveals Stellar Blade Studio Nearly Ran Out of Cash
items.s: Kim Hyung-tae, CEO of South Korean game studio Shift Up, says the company once had only about three months of payroll left while developing its hit console title Stellar Blade, as investors repeatedly doubted the project could recoup its costs.

items.t: Unitree Founder Says Robots Face a Millimetre-Scale Challenge
items.s: At Hangzhou's Global Digital Trade Expo, Unitree founder Wang Xingxing argued that humanoid robots still lack the precision for real work, and predicted a coming 'ChatGPT moment' for embodied AI once they can handle unfamiliar spaces.

items.t: Beijing Universal Adds Fast & Furious Ride as Five-Year Crowds Keep Growing
items.s: Beijing Universal Resort marked its fifth anniversary by announcing Asia's first Fast & Furious indoor ride and a new nighttime lake show. The park is doubling down on China even as global rivals slow their expansion.

items.t: Michelin's New Hotel Keys: Two Chinese Stays Reach Three Stars
items.s: Michelin's 2026 Keys list rates 2,832 hotels across 79 destinations, with Hong Kong's Rosewood and a Jiuzhaigou retreat holding three Keys and new Chinese properties climbing the ranks.

items.t: China's Audio Gear Makes Big Noise in Southeast Asia
items.s: From a small Shenzhen shop to 500,000 monthly sales in Southeast Asia, Chinese audio brands are thriving overseas by adapting products to local consumer needs.

items.t: China's Auto Industry Faces New Turn in Evolutionary Cycle
items.s: Four signals indicate China's car industry stands at the threshold of a new consolidation phase as market forces reshape the competitive landscape.

items.t: China's Lithium Battery Boom Faces Graphite Challenge
items.s: China's lithium battery industry announces 740,000 ton expansion amid concerns about graphite supply bottlenecks that could impact EV production.

items.t: Lithium Battery Market: Reality Meets Hype
items.s: While the market fears oversupply, lithium batteries remain紧缺. Two critical supply factors are being underestimated as demand continues to grow.

items.t: Traditional Meets Digital: China's Digital Museum Boom
items.s: China's cultural institutions are embracing digital technology to preserve and share ancient artifacts with global audiences, creating immersive experiences that bridge millennia.

items.t: 380,000 AI Dramas Later: China's Animation Gold Rush Hits Reality
items.s: Producers unleashed hundreds of thousands of AI-generated animated mini-dramas onto Chinese platforms this year, only to see payouts shrink and studios fold. As the bubble deflates, survivors are turning to lessons from Japan's 1980s anime boom for a way forward.

items.t: Feng Xiaogang's Box Office Flop Finds Redemption on Chinese Streaming
items.s: Dismissed at the Chinese box office, Feng Xiaogang's latest film has found its audience after moving to streaming, topping Tencent Video's heat rankings within days. The turnaround reignites a familiar debate about why China's pioneering commercial director keeps winning recognition only after the credits roll.

items.t: You Benchang, Beloved 'Ji Gong' Actor, Dies at 93
items.s: You Benchang, the Chinese actor whose tattered-robe portrayal of the legendary 'mad monk' Ji Gong charmed generations of viewers, has died in Beijing at 93. After decades of small stage roles, he found fame at 52 and won a new generation of fans at 90 in the hit drama 'Blossoms Shanghai.'

items.t: China's Digital Yuan Leading Global CBDC Race
items.s: China's digital currency is rapidly advancing with expanded pilot programs and growing merchant acceptance, positioning the nation at the forefront of central bank digital currency development worldwide.

items.t: China's 'Miracle Stock' Crashes 67% Just Days After IPO
items.s: Shengu Group, a veteran Chinese maker of giant industrial compressors, saw its shares collapse 67 percent within six days of a dazzling stock market debut. The whiplash offers a vivid lesson in the speculative frenzy gripping China's market for new listings.

items.t: China's Stock Market Soars While Investors Wonder
items.s: Despite two years of impressive gains, China's A-share market has created a puzzling scenario where indices have risen significantly while many individual investors report losses.

items.t: China's Two-Year Bull Market: Index Up 45%, Yet Investors Still Sigh
items.s: Two years after Chinese stocks rebounded from their September 2024 lows, the Shanghai Composite has climbed about 45 percent and market capitalization has swelled by roughly 51 trillion yuan. Yet many retail investors say their own accounts tell a far less celebratory story of widening wealth divergence.

items.t: Chinese Biotech Stock Soars 477% on Debut
items.s: Chinese biotech firm BaiRuiJi sees explosive 477% surge on first trading day after Beijing Stock Exchange listing, showcasing investor enthusiasm for healthcare innovation.

items.t: Chinese Company Wins $132M US Data Center Contract
items.s: Samsung Electric's Chinese subsidiary secures major US contract for data center transformers amid market volatility and stock fluctuations.

items.t: Chinese Transformer Maker Rides US Data Center Boom With $132 Million Order
items.s: Sanxing Electric, a Ningbo-based power equipment maker, surged its 10 percent daily limit after its subsidiary won a $132 million contract to supply oil-immersed transformers for a US data center energy storage project. The deal shows how the global AI building boom is pulling Chinese manufacturers into America's power infrastructure chain.

items.t: Chinese Game Combines Ancient Elements with Modern Match-3
items.s: New game 'Wuxing You' merges traditional Chinese five elements theory with popular match-3 gameplay, launching across multiple platforms with cross-platform multiplayer support.

items.t: Chinese Game Scene Thrives with Diverse Titles
items.s: China's gaming industry showcases its diversity with a VR courtroom drama, a hand-painted horror adventure, and a live-action interactive story, reflecting the country's growing creative output in the global gaming market.

items.t: Chinese Game 'Five Elements' Merges Ancient Philosophy with Modern Puzzle Battles
items.s: A new Chinese game combines traditional Five Elements theory with match-3 gameplay, creating a unique multiplayer experience across all devices.

items.t: Warhammer 40K: Dawn of War 4 Team Battle Report
items.s: Creative director and senior designer showcase 2v2 team gameplay in the upcoming Warhammer 40K: Dawn of War 4, revealing tactical insights for the December 3 release.

items.t: China's Coffee Culture Brewing Creative Home Mixes
items.s: Chinese coffee enthusiasts are crafting unique homemade beverages as specialty coffee culture grows nationwide, blending traditional flavors with modern techniques.

items.t: Here Wallpaper: Turning Places into Personalized Backgrounds
items.s: A new app transforms favorite locations into stunning wallpapers, allowing users to bring memories of home, travel destinations, or beloved natural scenes to their digital devices.

items.t: Vintage Computer Lab: A Decade of Tech Collection
items.s: From a business experiment to a cultural journey, one man's ten-year journey with vintage computers in China reveals how technology and passion converge.

items.t: China's Green Revolution in Agricultural Technology
items.s: China is pioneering sustainable farming solutions to feed its population while combating climate change, with innovations that could transform global agriculture.

items.t: China's Tennis Team Falls Short in Billie Jean King Cup Quarterfinals
items.s: China's tennis team lost 1-2 to defending champions Italy in the Billie Jean King Cup quarterfinals. Zheng Qinwen played through pain medication as China's quest for a semifinal spot ended at home.

items.t: China's Basketball Renaissance: From Courts to Global Stardom
items.s: China's basketball scene is experiencing unprecedented growth, producing NBA stars and hosting international competitions that showcase the nation's passion for the sport.

items.t: Japan Stuns China in Asian Games Table Tennis, Women Answer with Gold
items.s: Japan edged China 3-2 in a gripping men's team final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, denying the table tennis superpower a familiar crown. Hours later, China's women swept Japan 3-0 to win a sixth consecutive team title, restoring pride on a dramatic day in Nagoya.

items.t: Pain and Pride: China's Billie Jean King Cup Dream Ends in Shenzhen
items.s: Zheng Qinwen took the court on painkillers and fell to Jasmine Paolini as defending champions Italy edged China 2-1 in the Billie Jean King Cup quarterfinal in Shenzhen. Veteran Zhang Shuai had fired the hosts ahead, but Italy's depth proved decisive, sending the Italians into a semifinal against Ukraine.

items.t: Japan Ends 36-Year Chinese Reign in Asian Games Table Tennis Final
items.s: Japan's men stunned China 3-2 in the Asian Games team table tennis final in Nagoya, claiming their first gold in 60 years and ending a 36-year Chinese hold on the title. China's women responded with a 3-0 win over Japan for a sixth straight crown.

items.t: Table Tennis: China's National Passion
items.s: From schoolyards to Olympic glory, table tennis has become China's beloved national sport, uniting generations and showcasing the country's athletic excellence on the global stage.

items.t: China's EVs Prove More Reliable at High Mileage
items.s: British vehicle inspection data reveals electric vehicles perform better than gasoline cars after 90,000 miles, though with higher tire wear concerns.

items.t: China's MINISFORUM Trims Its Beloved Mini Workstation for Budget Buyers
items.s: Shenzhen mini PC maker MINISFORUM has launched a pared-down SE version of its MS-01 workstation, swapping premium 10-gigabit networking and modern memory for a lower price. The move shows how China's compact PC brands are now competing on choice, not just value.

items.t: Chinese EVs Outperform Gas Cars at High Mileages
items.s: New analysis of 47.4 million UK vehicle inspections reveals Chinese electric cars are more reliable than gasoline cars after 90,000 miles, challenging global perceptions of EV durability.

items.t: Global First: Massive Robot Theme Park Opens in China
items.s: China unveils world's largest embodied intelligence theme park featuring over 300 robots across diverse interactive scenarios, marking a milestone in human-robot collaboration.

items.t: BYD's Next-Gen Dolphin Interior Redefines EV Design
items.s: BYD unveils design sketches for its second-generation Dolphin model, featuring a revolutionary interior layout with relocated controls and innovative storage options.

items.t: GTA6 Collector Box Priced at $400
items.s: Rockstar Games launches a limited edition $400 collectible box for GTA6 without the actual game, featuring exclusive merchandise and memorabilia.

items.t: Samsung Smart Fridges Bricked After Update
items.s: Samsung's Bespoke AI refrigerators stop working after firmware updates, forcing users to discard food amid limited repair options during holidays.

items.t: Vivo Unveils X500 with Cutting-Edge MediaTek Processor
items.s: Chinese smartphone manufacturer vivo launches its latest flagship models featuring new MediaTek chips, continuing China's innovation in mobile technology.

items.t: Intel's LGA1954 Socket Revealed for Next-Gen Processors
items.s: Intel's upcoming LGA1954 socket components have surfaced online, signaling preparation for the Nova Lake-S processor series as part of Intel's desktop platform evolution.

items.t: Smartisan's Mocked TNT Workstation Looks Prescient in the AI Agent Era
items.s: Nearly eight years after Chinese startup Smartisan unveiled its ridiculed TNT workstation, former executive Li Nan says the device was simply ahead of its time. As AI agents now handle complex computer tasks from spoken instructions, the once-dismissed concept is winning quiet vindication.

items.t: Ancient Water Towns: China's Timeless Waterways
items.s: Explore China's enchanting ancient water towns, where canals replace streets and tradition blends seamlessly with modern tourism.

items.t: WeChat Sharpens HarmonyOS App With Inbox Tidying and Invoice Tools
items.s: Tencent has rolled out a new invite-only test build of WeChat for Huawei's HarmonyOS, letting users fold cluttering service accounts into a tidier view. The steady stream of updates signals how China's biggest super-app keeps deepening its roots in the homegrown operating system.

items.t: China's Tea Traditions in Modern Times
items.s: From ancient ceremonies to contemporary tea houses, China's 5,000-year tea culture continues to evolve while preserving its deep-rooted traditions.

items.t: The Ancient Art of Chinese Shadow Puppetry Meets Modern Light
items.s: Chinese shadow puppetry, a millennia-old storytelling tradition using intricately carved leather figures, is experiencing a cultural revival. Contemporary artists and theaters are preserving this UNESCO-recognized art form by blending classic tales with modern lighting and digital projection techniques.

items.t: Chinese Animation Industry Captures Global Imagination
items.s: China's animation sector has evolved from domestic productions to internationally acclaimed works, blending traditional cultural elements with cutting-edge technology to win global audiences.

items.t: Beats 360: Redefining Wireless Audio Experience
items.s: Apple's audio brand Beats unveils its first new over-ear headphones in three years, the Beats 360, combining premium sound with innovative design to mark two decades of audio innovation.

items.t: China's High-Speed Rail Network Connects Ancient and Modern
items.s: China's expanding high-speed rail network transforms travel across the world's most populous nation, connecting historic sites with modern cities at unprecedented speeds.

items.t: Marathon Madness: How Running Became China's Weekend Ritual
items.s: From mega-city marathons with lottery entry to trail races in the mountains, tens of millions of Chinese runners have turned weekend racing into a national pastime.

items.t: A Nation of Tea Drinkers Falls for Coffee
items.s: China now runs one of the world's largest coffee markets. From Shanghai's specialty roasters to app-driven chains, coffee has quietly become part of everyday urban life.

items.t: Seeing China at 350 km/h: A Practical High-Speed Rail Guide
items.s: With over 45,000 kilometers of high-speed lines linking megacities and ancient towns, China's bullet-train network is the fastest way for visitors to see the country. Here is how to use it.

items.t: Hanfu Revival: Young China Reclaims Traditional Dress
items.s: Flowing sleeves in city parks, hanfu photo studios and a multibillion-yuan market — traditional Chinese clothing has moved from costume play to everyday fashion.
